changes.current_line: Customers see an average uplift in authorization rates with Authorization Boost and Adaptive Acceptance.
changes.change: For ecommerce buyers who come in with checkout failures: 'Stop orders dying at the last step, especially on the big baskets. Here is what your failed orders are worth, and how much of that we can win back.' Put the prospect's own failure rate and its dollar value next to the line in place of the average uplift. Keep Authorization Boost and Adaptive Acceptance as the how, not the headline.
changes.why: We showed an average-uplift slide, but the champion described the problem in lost orders on expensive items from her own dashboard, and that problem was never turned into a dollar figure.

changes.change: When the CFO won't meet us and the champion is carrying the deal, give the champion a one-page business case she can hand over as-is. It should show the revenue lost to failed orders, our net cost after recovered orders compared with the incumbent's rate, and payback. Answer 'the same thing' on the page before the CFO says it: the rate is the same kind of cost, but the result is not, because fewer of your orders fail.
changes.why: The champion asked for 'a one-page business case' and received the deck and pricing. The CFO then decided from a rate-versus-rate page where our only input was our quote, and concluded he would not pay more 'for the same thing'.

changes.change: Proof-point offer for prospects who report checkout failures: 'Send us a three-month export of your declines and we'll show you what the failed orders were worth.' Make this a standard step before pricing, and use the result as the headline number in the business case.
changes.why: Our SE offered exactly this analysis on the customer's own data, which the incumbent could not explain, and it was skipped to protect quarter-end timing, leaving us with no customer-specific figure.

changes.current_line: Trusted by leading businesses; see our customer stories.
changes.change: When finance is the decider, use customer stories only as backup to the prospect's own declines figure, never as the main proof. Pair each story with the dollar value of recovered orders, not just the uplift.
changes.why: Customer stories and the average uplift were what we had to offer when the champion needed a business case for the CFO, and they never became a figure he could weigh.
